title: A Next static export served from S3
readWhen: reaching for a server feature — `headers()`, cookies, a proxy, a route handler — or wondering why this is Next rather than Vite
summary: Next.js with `output: 'export'`. `next build` writes HTML, JavaScript and CSS into `apps/myself-app/out`, and that directory is the whole deployment.

title: A static adapter behind entifix's repository port
readWhen: loading content, or tempted to import `@entifix/testing-unit` outside a spec
summary:
A read-only static adapter, written in this repository, implementing the public `EntityRepository` port.
`get` / `load` with the Mongo adapter's filter, sort and paging semantics, including array membership for `in` / `nin`.
`save` / `delete` fail with a typed `EntifixLogicError`.
Records arrive as JSON and are validated from each entity's metadata before they are served; a failure fails `next build`.
Links resolve through `EntityLinkResolverTag`.

title: Pages render at build; interactive parts query in the browser
readWhen: a component needs data, or a page's client bundle grew
summary:
A — static content is loaded at build time.
C — interactive parts load in the browser.
C is where a backend slots in later.

title: An Nx workspace: app, domain, static adapter, content
readWhen: adding a package or an import between two, or putting an entity class somewhere
summary:
The adapter knows no entity.
Content is its own package.
Boundaries are enforced by `nx.tags` and `@nx/enforce-module-boundaries`, replacing the old app's per-folder `no-restricted-imports` lists (#18).

title: English and Spanish, with localized content fields
readWhen: adding copy or content, or when a translation is missing
summary:
`en` and `es`, `en` by default.
Routes carry the locale.
UI copy lives in catalogs, and a key present in one locale only fails the build (#17).
Content uses localized fields.
The page picks the language.

title: Tailwind v4 and everything `@entifix/style` involves
readWhen: styling anything, or when a primitive renders unstyled
summary:
Tailwind v4, CSS-first, with `@entifix/style/tokens.css` and its palette presets, each scoped to `[data-theme]` on `<html>`.
Layout and atoms come from `@entifix/react-controls/primitives`.
The main barrel of `@entifix/react-controls` is never imported.
`./primitives` goes through `optimizePackageImports`.
The theme is applied before first paint.

title: Hosting is deferred; the build stays host-neutral
readWhen: a URL works in `next dev` but not in the export, or when choosing where the site is served from
summary:
`trailingSlash: true`, so `/en/cv` is written as `en/cv/index.html`.
A `404.html` at the root of the export.
Served from the domain root.
No redirects or rewrites.
`/` redirects in the page.

title: A landing page of five static sections
readWhen: adding or reordering a landing section, or when the in-page nav or the language switch loses its place
summary:
Five sections, in this order: hero, about, projects, entifix, contact.
The hero is typography-led, and does not move.
The section nav is anchors first.
The language switch keeps the section only when scripting is on.
Headings are copy, facts are content.

title: The radar's maths is ported, and it runs at build time
readWhen: the radar's blips moved between two builds, or a radar library is
summary:
The geometry and layout are ported to TypeScript, and they run during `next build`.
The port lives in the incubator's radar control.
The radar ships no JavaScript.
The force simulation is not ported.
The control knows no semantics.

title: Content is checked from entity metadata, and every package ships `dist`
readWhen: a record fails `next build`, a member should be translated, a filter over a list matches nothing, or a package's code reaches the app as source
summary:
Validation reads `describeEntityColumns` — the resolved metadata, every default applied — and nothing else about an entity.
Localized members are a list beside the classes.
Rules the metadata cannot express are registered by the app.
No localized or collection member is `filterable` or `sortable`.
The read half of the contract is re-created.

title: A moving hero, a revealing nav and a blue theme
readWhen: the hero's motion or the nav's reveal misbehaves with scripting off or reduced motion, a first visit paints a theme you did not expect, or a printed CV comes out dark
summary:
The hero moves, in CSS only.
The hero shows no tagline.
Reduced motion turns every animation off.
One navigation bar. The section anchors (about, projects, entifix, contact), the CV, the radar, a language menu and a theme menu share one bar.
Language and theme are dropdowns, on native `<details>`.

title: The CV as a paper sheet, in variants and two modes
readWhen: a CV page spills onto a second page, an applicant tracking system reads the PDF wrong, a variant shows the wrong bullets, a CV URL 404s under `serve-out`, or the printed sheet differs from the screen
summary:
Variants. A `CvVariant` is a reading of the same career: its title and summary, the technologies it lists, the employments it shows, and the _focuses_ it takes.
Focuses select the bullets.
The sheet adds education, certificates and a location.
Two modes, both static.
Neither mode uses two columns, a photo, skill bars, or text in a header or footer.

title: CloudFront over a private bucket, defined in Pulumi, released on every merge
readWhen: a URL answers differently on `herbercolop.dev` than under `serve-out`, a deploy shipped stale HTML, a merge to `main` did not deploy, or an infrastructure change is being made by hand in the console
summary:
CloudFront in front of a private S3 bucket.
A CloudFront Function on viewer request.
An ACM certificate for the apex and `www`, validated by DNS in the existing hosted zone.
Cache-Control is set per object at upload.
The domain and its hosted zone are not in the stack.

title: A personal radar: rings for one person, editions in content, filtering over placed blips
readWhen: a blip shows the wrong movement, a ring's meaning is questioned, a technology needs its own page, or the radar's filter is about to query in the browser
summary:
Rings, for one person.
Quadrants stay Thoughtworks' four.
Movement is measured against an edition in content.
A static page per technology.
Filtering dims blips the build already placed.

title: Customizing the CV in the browser: the URL holds what is hidden, a stylesheet hides it
readWhen: a customized CV flashes its hidden parts on load, loses a choice on reload, in print or after switching reading, or the customizer is about to query content in the browser
summary:
The server renders everything; a stylesheet hides.
The URL holds the choices.
Hidden before the first paint.
The controls are plain props.
Human sheet only. The ATS pages carry no parts, no script and no controls: what a parser reads stays exactly what was built.

title: entifix queries run in the browser too: one use case, two repositories
readWhen: a filter or a list in the browser needs data, a page's scripts grew past its budget, a filtered view disagrees with the page it filters, or code is about to move into entifix
summary:
The same use case answers a page and a filter.
The query string declares its parameters.
The static HTML stays the unfiltered page.
Two filtering rules are Mongo's, in the static adapter.
An incubator layer holds what is meant for entifix.

title: A blog of Markdown posts on entities
readWhen: adding or editing a post, a post fails `next build`, a draft appears in the export, a post's image or link breaks, or the blog's filter shows the wrong posts
summary:
A post is an entity.
Bodies are Markdown files beside the records.
Markdown with directives, not MDX.
Images and links are checked at build.
Drafts are for `next dev`.

title: The incubator owns content mechanics; the app declares sources and rules
readWhen: a loader builds an id → record map or casts a link, a new entity needs a source, a content rule is about to be written by hand, a page's filter is about to be wired again, or code is about to move into entifix
summary:
Content is defined once, in the incubator.
Link targets come from metadata.
A load resolves the links it is asked to.
Generic rules are factories.
A source's published view is typed.

title: Layered packages: domain, content, entifix-incubator, implementation
readWhen: a file is about to be added and it is not obvious which package it belongs in, a component is about to load content or read a site class it does not own, a page's filter needs its data, a boundary lint error names `layer:implementation`, or code is about to move into entifix
summary:
Packages are grouped by layer, and named from their folders.
The domain holds the business: entities, use cases, rules.
The implementation layer wires the domain to a delivery mechanism, in two kinds that never import each other.
What a component may reach depends on its level.
A filter's data arrives through a context.

title: Project pages, and decision records as content
readWhen: a record in `docs/adr` changed and the site still shows the old one, the conventions spec says the ADR copies drift, a project's page is about to show something its repository does not have, a record fails `next build`, or a Spanish reader asks why the records are in English
summary:
A featured project has a page.
Records are content. `ArchitectureDecision` is an entity (#77); `tools/sync-adrs.mjs` copies each repository's `docs/adr` into `packages/content/src/adrs.json`…
This repository's copies cannot drift.
Records stay in English.
The file tree is written by hand.

title: A changelog committed by the release
readWhen: `CHANGELOG.md` is missing a release or disagrees with its GitHub Release, the release job cannot push to `main`, a deploy shipped a commit that is not the squash commit, or `main` gained a `chore: release` commit nobody wrote
summary:
The release writes `CHANGELOG.md`.
A GitHub App pushes it.
The deploy ships the release commit.
`[skip ci]` keeps the commit from deploying twice.

title: The tier contract, and the seam a host configures across
readWhen: adding a package, adding a dependency between two, deciding whether something is public API, or about to bake a host's value into framework code — a downward edge can still be illegal, and the seam takes values rather than paths
summary:
`i18n` is T2, not T0.
`testing-*` is T5, above everything.
A downward edge can still be illegal.
The subpath is not decoration — it is the part that works.
An exemption is named one at a time, with its reason on the line.

title: entifix is MIT, and the trigger that would freeze that choice
readWhen: publishing a package, accepting an outside contribution, or wondering whether the licence can still be changed — a shipped version's grant is permanent, the project's licence going forward is not
summary:
entifix is MIT. It is the simplest licence that makes the project open source, it is what the manifest already claimed, and every external dependency in the…
§3, an express patent grant.
§6, an explicit trademark withholding.
That ends with the first outside contribution.

title: Releasing without a credential, and the version a commit is allowed to cut
readWhen: cutting a release, wondering why the release workflow cannot be renamed, or why a merge did not publish anything — the version is derived from commit messages and nothing in this repository can publish to npm
summary:
Nothing in this repository can publish to npm.
`.github/workflows/release.yml` cannot be renamed.
A release is a pull request.
The branch is named for the version, so a version change opens a second pull request.
Publishing waits for a person.

title: The examples are the composability proof, and one of them gates every pull request
readWhen: adding an example, adding an e2e journey, putting an entity class inside a Next application, or wondering why a verb declared with `@useCase()` never appears on screen — entity classes need SWC's 2022-03 decorators, which Next's own compiler cannot provide
summary:
Turbopack panics in its decorator transform — `not implemented: ClassMember::PrivateProp` — on the `#field` every entity declares, and reports it as `Module…
webpack (`next build --webpack`) does not parse the decorator at all: `Expression expected` at `@entity(`.
That package is `sideEffects: true`, and it has to be.
